transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

I’ve been feeling really overwhelmed because I'm convinced that people are constantly watching and monitoring me. It feels like there is some kind of organization tracking my every move, and I just can't shake this belief.

Have you also had periods of major depression or mania—like feeling very down or hopeless, or unusually energized, needing little sleep, and feeling unusually confident—at the same time as these beliefs, or have the beliefs happened only by themselves?

I've had long periods of feeling deeply depressed and exhausted at the same time as these beliefs, but I have never experienced those highly energized or manic states. However, there have also been times lasting at least a couple of weeks where I still felt monitored and heard things even when my mood wasn't particularly low.
During the times when your mood was not low, did you also have trouble with work, school, self-care, or becoming more withdrawn or emotionally flat?

Yes, even when I wasn't feeling particularly down, I still felt completely numb and flat emotionally. I ended up withdrawing from my family and friends, and I had no motivation to handle my work or even basic daily tasks. It just felt impossible to get myself moving or care about anything.
About how long have the hallucinations or paranoid beliefs lasted when your depression was not present—days, weeks, months, or longer?

Those experiences usually lasted for about two to three weeks at a time when I wasn't feeling depressed. During those periods, the feeling of being monitored and hearing things would still be fully there. It was really draining, even without the low mood.

Have there also been any times when the hallucinations or paranoid beliefs lasted for at least two weeks while you had no depression at all, or has every episode of psychosis always happened only during depression?

Yes, there have definitely been times lasting at least two weeks where I felt monitored and heard things with no depression at all. During those periods, my mood felt completely normal, but the tracking and the voices were still fully happening. It wasn't tied to being depressed.
Based on what you've described, the psychotic symptoms have occurred for at least two weeks without depression, which makes schizophrenia more likely than schizoaffective disorder.

I understand your observation, and it's true I've had those periods of hearing voices and feeling monitored for a couple of weeks without being depressed. However, the severe depression has still been a massive, overwhelming part of my life for almost these entire two years. What does the distinction between those two diagnoses actually mean for my treatment?
Over the full two years, have the depressive episodes been present for the majority of the illness, or have the psychotic symptoms been present for most of the time even when your mood was okay?

The depression has definitely been present for the vast majority of these past two years, making up most of the time I've been struggling. However, there were still those specific periods of at least a couple of weeks where my mood felt relatively normal, yet the voices and tracking were still happening. It has mostly been a constant state of depression, but those symptoms did occur on their own during those brief windows.

This pattern is most consistent with schizoaffective disorder, depressive type, because the depression has been present for most of the illness and there have also been at least two weeks of psychosis without depression.

That explanation makes a lot of sense, and it really matches what I've been going through over the last year and eleven months. It is honestly a relief to have a clear name for this combination of constant depression and those episodes. Knowing what this is makes me feel a bit more hopeful about getting the right help.
